title: Mental models as skill-map nodes
statement: Should a skill map name, as nodes of their own, the mental models its operations presuppose, such as a text being made for a purpose or claims needing support?
detail: A proposed change to a Grade 5 reading skill graph of 47 skills notes that it names operations, schemas, facts and exam mechanics but none of the mental models the operations presuppose, and adds an audit step asking, for each operation, what model must already be in place for it to be teachable and whether the graph names it. Its candidates are a text as a made thing whose content, order and emphasis were chosen for a purpose, and claims as things that need support and can lack it. The proposal says such models are built through coordinated examples rather than stated, and that without them the graph declares students ready when their mental model is not.
against: It is a proposal only: the graph was not modified, and no result of the audit is recorded (`grade3-reading/artifacts/semantic-judge-calibration-2026-07-10/kc-graph-change-proposal.md`, lines 9-12).

evidence.quote: **text as authored artifact** - a text is a made thing whose author chose content, order, and emphasis for a purpose; presupposed by infer_point_of_view, disc_reasons_and_evidence, and every source-attribution construction, captured by none of them.
The audit asks, per operation in the closed vocabulary: what mental model must already be in place for this operation to be teachable, and does the graph name it as a node?
Without them the graph declares students ready when their mental model is not.
